variant_scope.value: Primary target: M5 Competition, 460 kW / 625 PS. Pre-LCI (production 07/2018-06/2020, US MY2019-2020) and LCI (production 07/2020-06/2023, US MY2021-2023) values are both given where they differ; the LCI car is the default for the builder.
variant_scope.note: Production months: LCI 07/2020 start from ADAC catalogue, end 06/2023 from auto motor und sport 'Baujahr 07/2020 bis 06/2023'. Pre-LCI Competition start month is an assumption (press release 06 Aug 2018, photos dated 05/2018).

brief_checks.claim: Engine S63B44T4, 4.4 L twin-turbo hot-V V8, 617 hp / 625 PS
brief_checks.detail: BMW NA 2021 spec table lists engine type S63B44T4; 4,395 cc; 460 kW = 625 PS (EU) = 617 hp (US SAE). Turbos sit inside the 90-degree V. Base (non-Competition) M5 is 441 kW / 600 PS / 600 hp.

ZF 8HP-family torque-converter automatic with Drivelogic (3 shift programs) and an oil cooler. BMW parts catalogue (via Wikipedia) lists GA8HP75Z for the pre-LCI car; BMW NA lists 'M8HP76' for the 2021 LCI. Gear ratios are identical.

brief_checks.claim: M xDrive with 4WD, 4WD Sport and 2WD modes, Active M Differential
brief_checks.detail: Five configurations: DSC on = 4WD only; MDM (M Dynamic Mode) = 4WD Sport; DSC off = 4WD, 4WD Sport or 2WD. 2WD is only available with DSC off. Rear-biased; centre multi-plate clutch; Active M Differential (rear, electronically controlled multi-plate, 0-100 % locking).

brief_checks.claim: (not in brief) commonly repeated errors found while checking
brief_checks.detail: Compression ratio is 10.0:1 (BMW), not 10.5:1. Final drive is 3.154 (BMW EU) / 3.15 (BMW NA); auto motor und sport data pages print 2.93, which conflicts with BMW and with parts listings (3.15) - treat 2.93 as an error. Wikipedia's '0-100 km/h 3.1 s' for the Competition is the US 0-60 mph claim; BMW's 0-100 km/h is 3.3 s. Reverse ratio differs between BMW sheets (3.478 EU, 3.38 US 2021, 4.172 US 2017 preliminary).
brief_checks.sources: bmw_spec_092018; bmw_spec_062020; bmwna_2021; bmwna_2018_spec; ams_2021_e63; wiki_m5

full_load_torque_curve_chart_nodes.note: READ FROM CHART: BMW 06/2020 'Output and torque diagrams', M5 Competition (460 kW). The PDF chart is vector art; the curve vertices were extracted from the drawing paths and mapped to the axis grid (error well under 1 %). The curve is a polyline through these nodes. The power curve on the same chart agrees with torque x rpm to within 0.5 kW at every node. Crank figures (manufacturer net output), not wheel.

full_load_torque_curve_500rpm.note: READ FROM CHART at 500 rpm steps by linear interpolation between the chart nodes above; 2,000-5,500 rpm plateau rounded to the published 750 Nm. 7,200 rpm is where BMW's curve ends (cut-off).

full_load_power_curve_500rpm.note: READ FROM CHART (power curve on the same diagram).

torque_below_1000rpm.note: Not on BMW's chart. 400 Nm at 1,000 rpm equals about 11.4 bar BMEP, i.e. roughly naturally-aspirated full load with little boost; extended down at similar volumetric efficiency with a mild fall-off at very low speed.

redline.note: BMW NA M5 CS release (same S63B44T4): 'engine redline is 7,200 rpm'. BMW's M5 Competition power/torque chart ends at 7,200 rpm.

limiter_cutoff.note: BMW S63TU training manual lists 'cutoff speed 7200 rpm' for the F10 M5's S63TU; Wikipedia: rev limit raised from 6,800 (S63) to 7,200. BMW: in manual mode there is no automatic upshift at the limiter (bmwna_2018_pr; bmw_lci_pr_ie_2020). Limiter style (hard fuel cut vs soft ignition cut) not published.

idle_rpm.note: Not published. Typical warm idle for BMW N63/S63 V8s is about 550-650 rpm; cold-start fast idle is higher (estimate 1,000-1,300 rpm for the first tens of seconds). Verify against the Commons start-up recording or a video with a visible tachometer.

launch_control_rpm.note: Not published. Launch control exists (The Drive 2021 mentions initiating launch control). Estimate based on a torque-converter launch that must pre-build boost (full torque arrives at 1,800 rpm) without overwhelming 4WD traction; plausible range 2,500-3,500 rpm. Verify on an onboard launch video.

firing_order.note: From BMW's S63TU (F10 M5) technical training manual data table, which lists 1-5-4-8-6-3-7-2 for both the S63 and S63TU. The cross-bank manifold of the F90's S63TU4 (BMW spec 'cross-bank exhaust manifold') only works with this order, so carry-over is near certain [assumption].

cylinder_numbering.value: BMW convention: cylinder 1 is at the front of the RIGHT bank (right = passenger side on a left-hand-drive car, seen in the direction of travel). Right bank = cylinders 1, 2, 3, 4 front to rear; left bank = cylinders 5, 6, 7, 8 front to rear.
cylinder_numbering.note: BMW manual: 'exhaust manifold ... in driving direction, 1st cylinder, top right'; 'cylinder bank 1-4 (R)', 'cylinder bank 5/8 (L)'.

firing_events_deg.unit: [cylinder, crank degrees after cyl 1 TDC-firing, bank]
firing_events_deg.note: Derived: even 90-degree firing intervals across the engine (720/8). Per-bank intervals are uneven, the classic cross-plane pattern: right bank 180-270-180-90 degrees, left bank 180-90-180-270 degrees. The cross-bank manifold regroups the pulses so each turbo sees even 180-degree spacing (see forced_induction).

firing_frequency.note: Engine order 4 (crank). Each exhaust branch after a turbo carries order 2.

lubrication.value: Wet sump with small front sump chamber, fully variable map-controlled oil pump (suction pump for the front chamber), designed for track g-loads; extra engine-oil cooler

cooling.value: Separate circuits for engine/turbochargers and for the indirect charge-air coolers; electric pump keeps coolant flowing through the turbochargers after shut-off

engine_mounts.note: Competition-specific mounts; BMW NA: 5,139 lb/in (Competition/CS) vs 3,312 lb/in (about 580 N/mm) for the standard M5.

placement.value: Hot-V: both turbochargers inside the 90-degree V on top of the engine, one positioned over each cylinder bank; turbines exhaust rearward into close-coupled catalysts
placement.note: Positions from the F10 S63TU manual ('turbocharger installed over cylinder bank 5/8 (L)' and 'over cylinder bank 1-4 (R)'). Catalyst position also S63TU [assumption for TU4].

value.principle: Four-into-two-per-turbo, overlapping 'cross-bank' manifold: each turbo is fed by two cylinders from EACH bank, chosen so that the turbo receives a pulse every 180 crank degrees, like an inline-4; each scroll receives a pulse every 360 degrees.

cross_bank_manifold.note: BMW S63TU manual: 'exhaust gas pulses from cylinders 1/6 and 4/7 are fed to the exhaust turbocharger installed over cylinder bank 5/8 (L) and the exhaust gas from cylinders 2/8 and 3/5 is fed to the exhaust turbocharger installed over cylinder bank 1-4 (R)'; '360 degrees of crankshaft angle between the two exhaust cycles within the exhaust flute'. Manifold figure legend: 2/8 right front scroll, 3/5 right rear scroll, 1/6 left front scroll, 4/7 left rear scroll. F90 retains a cross-bank manifold (BMW 2017/2020: 'cross-bank exhaust manifolds ... modified to optimise the flow of energy to the turbine wheels'). Pulse times derived from the firing order.

max_boost_relative_base_M5.note: = 1.69 bar gauge. Stated for the 600 hp M5 at launch (Aug 2017). For comparison the F10 M5's S63TU ran 1.5 bar (Wikipedia, P).

max_boost_relative_competition.note: Not published. Same 750 Nm torque as the base M5 but held to higher rpm and 19 kW more peak power, so slightly more boost at the top end: estimate 1.7-1.8 bar gauge. Verify with logged data from owners.

boost_onset_rpm.note: From the chart: 400 Nm at 1,000 rpm is about naturally aspirated full load (11.4 bar BMEP), so boost starts building at roughly 1,000-1,200 rpm; torque rises steeply from 1,244 rpm (480 Nm) to 1,500 (600 Nm).

full_boost_rpm.note: Full 750 Nm from 1,800 rpm (steady-state full load). In a transient from low load, expect several tenths of a second of spool in higher gears [E].

boost_taper.value: Above about 5,860 rpm torque falls (733 Nm at 6,000, 647 at 6,600, 587 at 7,000, 564 at 7,200) while power stays within 460-425 kW: boost is tapered toward the cut-off.

wastegate.value: One wastegate per turbo. S63TU (F10): vacuum-actuated through an electro-pneumatic pressure converter. S63TU4 actuation type not confirmed.
wastegate.note: Gap for the F90: the BMW TU4 training manual (ST1916) was not reachable.

blow_off_valve.value: None. BMW: the S63TU 'does not use a blow-off valve. The use of Valvetronic and special tuning rendered it unnecessary'; compressors were redesigned so they are 'not sensitive to pump' (surge).
blow_off_valve.note: Carry-over to TU4 assumed. Audio implication: no blow-off 'pssh' on lift-off; at most a faint compressor flutter, mostly masked.

charge_air_cooling.value: Indirect (water-to-air) charge-air coolers, about 20 % smaller yet more effective than the previous M5's

engine_order_summary.value: Cross-plane V8, even 90-degree firing; firing order 1-5-4-8-6-3-7-2; cylinders 1-4 right bank, 5-8 left bank (cyl 1 front right)

value: Hot-V: exhaust ports face into the V; two cross-bank 4-into-2 manifolds (each pairs cylinders from both banks: 1/6 + 4/7 to the turbo over the left bank, 2/8 + 3/5 to the turbo over the right bank).
Two twin-scroll turbines inside the V; each turbine sees an even pulse every 180 deg (inline-4-like), the two turbines offset by 90 deg.
One close-coupled catalyst directly after each turbine (S63TU: double-walled, two ceramic monoliths; assumed carried over).
EU cars (Competition from 2018, and the LCI): gasoline particulate filter(s) (BMW: 'addition of a particulate filter'; ADAC: Otto-Partikelfilter). Number and position not published.
Dual-branch (two separate pipes, one per turbo) M Sport exhaust; Helmholtz resonator between the two rear silencers (saves 5 kg).
Electrically actuated exhaust flaps (BMW NA, M5 CS text, same M Sport system) controlled by EFFICIENT / SPORT / SPORT+; M Sound Control button forces the quiet setting.
Four tailpipes, two each side; Competition tips in black chrome (LCI: thinner walls).

acoustic_consequence_of_cross_bank_manif.value: Each tailpipe branch carries one turbo's even 180-degree pulse train (engine order 2 per branch, order 4 combined), so the classic cross-plane 'burble' (half-order content from uneven per-bank firing) is largely removed before the exhaust leaves the engine bay. Expect a smoother, more 'even' V8 note than a log-manifold cross-plane V8, with turbine and catalyst muffling; uneven character survives mainly at idle and on overrun.
acoustic_consequence_of_cross_bank_manif.note: Engineering inference from BMW's manifold description; useful for synthesis: weight orders 4 and 8 strongly, add weaker orders 2 and 6 per branch, keep 0.5-order components low except at idle.

turbo_sound.value: No blow-off valve (S63TU design, assumed carried over), so no 'pssh' on lift. Reviewers report essentially no lag; turbo whistle is subdued on the stock car.
turbo_sound.note: Suggest a quiet broadband spool/whistle layer rising with boost, peaking 1,800-4,000 rpm under load, and a faint flutter on sudden lift at high boost.

value.note: C/D: Sport mode plays an enhanced engine soundtrack through the audio system. Idle figure not in the repost.
auto motor und sport interior noise ('Innengeraeusch'), automatic in D.
Compiled figure, original source not identified; snippet only.

car_and_driver_competition_dBA.note: GAP: no Car and Driver sound figures for the M5 Competition were reachable. Estimate from C/D's base M5 (66 / 74-80) and auto motor und sport's LCI Competition (idle 48, max 81, 71 dB(A) at 130 km/h); the Competition's louder M Sport exhaust and stiffer mounts add a little.

eu_stationary_noise.note: Manufacturer value quoted by auto motor und sport ('Stand-/Fahrgeraeusch 86 / 71 dB(A)').

eu_stationary_noise_test_rpm.note: Not printed with the F90 value. UN R51.03 stationary test uses 3,750 rpm for engines whose rated-power speed is 5,000-7,500 rpm (here 6,000); BMW lists the current G90 M5 as 88 dB(A) at 3,750 rpm. Rule quoted from memory of R51.03 - verify.

eu_pass_by_noise.note: Manufacturer value via auto motor und sport. ADAC lists 72 dB for the LCI M5 Competition (07/20-09/20) - 1 dB discrepancy, possibly a later homologation.

active_sound_design.value: Yes. The F90 has an Active Sound Design (ASD) control unit (BMW parts listings). Car and Driver: 'Switch to Sport mode and the audio system plays an enhanced version of the engine's soundtrack'; its sound meter peaked at 80 dB(A) in Sport versus 74 dB(A) at full throttle in the default mode. BMW's description of M5 ASD (F10 launch, 2011): synthesised from the engine's firing sequence and the exhaust's frequency range, adapts to the selected engine mode, spread evenly to all five seats. LCI TRACK mode mutes the audio system.
active_sound_design.note: Share of speaker-generated sound: NOT PUBLISHED. The 6 dB Sport-mode rise includes the exhaust flaps opening, so ASD adds at most about 6 dB at full throttle in Sport/Sport+ [E]; at cruise in Comfort/Efficient it is mild. For the game cabin mix: a clean, low-order 'ASD' layer (orders 2, 4, 8 of crank speed, smooth envelope tied to load) that is louder in SPORT/SPORT+ and absent in TRACK.

limiter_behaviour.value: Fuel/ignition cut at about 7,200 rpm. In manual mode the gearbox does not upshift, so the engine bounces on the limiter; in D it upshifts just before.
limiter_behaviour.note: Cut style and bounce rate not published; suggest a 10-15 Hz bounce of about 150-250 rpm [E].

value.EFFICIENT_or_M_Sound_Control: flaps closed, essentially no pops; soft burble only
value.SPORT: flaps open under load; occasional light burble on lift-off
value.SPORT_PLUS: most overrun burble, 'booms and snaps' on lift-off, strongest in lower gears (reviewer: hold 2nd in Sport+ and lift)
value.EU_OPF_effect: OPF-equipped EU cars crackle less sharply than US cars [estimate]

overrun_pops_by_mode.note: Mode behaviour inferred from BMW's flap/mode description and reviewer reports; not a BMW statement.

upshift_character.value: Torque-converter automatic: quick, smooth upshifts in Drivelogic 1-2; Drivelogic 3 and launch-control upshifts are firmer ('decently jolty'). No ignition-cut 'bark' like a dual-clutch; a short torque dip is heard.
upshift_character.note: Synthesis: shift cut 60-120 ms, small level dip, little crack.

the M5 settles into a quiet idle that's perhaps a bit too quiet from the inside.
Put the transmission into Sport +, hold it in second, then let off the gas for a very yummy burble.
that insanely menacing exhaust note lets people know that this is no ordinary BMW.
The exhaust is mellow (at least from inside the cabin).
Switch to Sport mode and the audio system plays an enhanced version of the engine's soundtrack.
At speed, the V8 sounds throaty with an aggressive crackle that brings to mind a phlegm-congested dragon.
